newsitem.title: RUSSIA: CSFB buys 3 pct of Russian Bank Vozrozhdeniye.
newsitem.headline: CSFB buys 3 pct of Russian Bank Vozrozhdeniye.

text.p: One of Russia's biggest banks, AKB Vozrozhdeniye, has sold three percent of its shares through an American Depositary Receipts (ADR) programme to investment bank CS First Boston, Vozrozhdeniye said on Thursday.
One ADR corresponds to one underlying ordinary share with a face value of 10,000 roubles.
Vozrozhdeniye Deputy Chairman Alexander Dolgopolov told a news conference that CSFB paid 20,000 roubles for each ADR.
ING Bank Eurasia is the custodian and the Bank of New York is the depositary bank in the deal.
Another big Russian bank, Inkombank, issued ADRs for three percent of its shares and Bank Menatep is planning an ADR issue.

Russian bank shares, except for shares in state-owned savings bank Sberbank, are highly illiquid. Russia has imposed bureaucratic hurdles on foreign shareholding in local banks and promised to limit ADR issues.
